purpose: Build a shared AI vocabulary that lets operators, administrators, engineers, leaders, and vendors discuss the same system without using one word for five different things.
staffSummary: Build M03 around one consequential utility situation and one decision: Choose the precise term needed to describe a model, product, input, output, source, tool, or workflow in a utility conversation. The learner must leave with a usable One Water AI vocabulary field guide, not a collection of definitions.
openingSituation: A project meeting stalls because the vendor says model, the utility hears product, the engineer means algorithm, and procurement thinks the term names the complete service.
learnerDecision: Choose the precise term needed to describe a model, product, input, output, source, tool, or workflow in a utility conversation.
analogy: The legend on a utility map gives every color and line a shared meaning. A technical vocabulary should do the same for an AI system.
learnerOutcomes: Explain The Lexicon of AI: Every Term, Every Token in plain English and connect it to a real water, wastewater, stormwater, or One Water decision.
Distinguish model, product, token, prompt, context, parameter, output, tool, and workflow without using one term to hide several different jobs.
Analyze the module situation, identify missing evidence, and name the professional consequence of a weak decision.
Compare how the same question changes across drinking water, wastewater, stormwater, administration, engineering, finance, technology, and public leadership.

Evaluate sources, assumptions, limitations, permissions, and human authority using this boundary: Keep model names, context windows, prices, and product features dated and verified. Do not teach changing product details as permanent definitions.
Create a usable One Water AI vocabulary field guide with evidence, roles, limits, review steps, and the next accountable action.
Defend the recommendation to Foundation, Practitioner, and Leader audiences while keeping disagreement and uncertainty visible.
curriculumOutcomes: Give The Lexicon of AI: Every Term, Every Token one clear learning job inside Foundations and Mental Models.
Connect the module to a consequential decision and the One Water AI vocabulary field guide.
Preserve current content, proposals, enhancements, and contributor records by stable identifier.
Separate verified evidence, Hardeep positions, expert interpretation, instructional scenarios, and unresolved questions.
Create an explicit bridge to the preceding and following modules without duplicating their work.
marketingOutcomes: Describe the practical value as helping a learner make and explain this decision: Choose the precise term needed to describe a model, product, input, output, source, tool, or workflow in a utility conversation.
Name the One Water AI vocabulary field guide as the visible result of the module.
Do not promise savings, compliance, certification, safety, performance, implementation success, or career outcomes without separately approved evidence.
requiredWorkProduct: One Water AI vocabulary field guide
definitionOfDone: The learner explains the core distinctions, completes the required evidence and decision activities, passes distributed checks, saves a complete One Water AI vocabulary field guide, and names the next accountable action.
scopeBoundary: Keep model names, context windows, prices, and product features dated and verified. Do not teach changing product details as permanent definitions.
